briefs.headline: Sunderland beat Chelsea 1-0 on a Le Fee penalty, and Chelsea drop out of the top four
briefs.summary: Enzo Le Fee converted in the 36th minute at the Stadium of Light after Levi Colwill brought down Brian Brobbey in the area, and Chelsea, with most of the second-half possession, forced four saves from Robin Roefs; Cole Palmer was bundled over earlier, but a VAR check placed the contact outside the box. It was Sunderland's first league win since August and Chelsea's fourth league defeat, leaving them 5th on 16 points, two behind Liverpool, going into the international break; Leeds visit Stamford Bridge on Saturday, Nov. 21, at 10 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Liverpool beat Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park and climb to 4th
briefs.summary: Alexis Mac Allister headed in Dominik Szoboszlai's free kick in the 40th minute, Florian Wirtz turned in Bradley Barcola's low cross in the 54th for his first league goal of the season, and Alexander Isak's deflected finish in the 89th made it three before Eddie Nketiah's stoppage-time penalty; Alisson made six saves and Palace hit the bar through Yeremy Pino and had a Jorgen Strand Larsen goal ruled offside. Liverpool have 18 points from 10 matches and host Manchester United on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 11:30 a.m. ET; Palace are bottom on 7.

briefs.headline: Tottenham back Leeds' complaint of racist abuse aimed at Bogle after Saturday's match
briefs.summary: Leeds said Sunday that defender Jayden Bogle, whose studs caught Mathys Tel's Achilles in a challenge the referee and VAR let stand in Saturday's win over Tottenham, was subjected to racist abuse on social media, and that the club will work with the Premier League and the authorities to identify those responsible; Tottenham said they were disgusted and offered Leeds their support, and the Premier League said anyone found guilty faces club bans and prosecution. PA reported that Tottenham will write to Pro Ref, the referees' body, to ask why Bogle was not sent off, and the club is awaiting the extent of Tel's injury.

briefs.headline: Burrow throws 3 TD passes as the Bengals beat the Falcons 34-17 in Madrid
briefs.summary: Joe Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards, hit Ja'Marr Chase for a 47-yard score and Tee Higgins twice, and ran in from the 1 as Cincinnati scored on every first-half possession at the Bernabeu before a crowd of 78,660; Chase caught 10 passes for 155 yards, 142 of them before halftime. The Bengals have won four straight and scored 30 or more in each, tying a franchise record from 1997, and host Pittsburgh on Sunday night; Bijan Robinson ran for 100 yards and a touchdown for Atlanta, which lost its second straight.

briefs.headline: Saints beat the Browns 23-22 in overtime after Cleveland's 2-point try fails
briefs.summary: Tyler Shough's 15-yard touchdown pass to Juwan Johnson opened overtime, Shedeur Sanders answered with a 39-yard touchdown to Harold Fannin Jr. with a minute left, and Todd Monken went for two and the win rather than a tying kick; Sanders rolled right under pressure from Carl Granderson and threw incomplete. Sanders, starting for Deshaun Watson, was 19 of 31 for 297 yards with a 64-yard score to KC Concepcion and a 30-yard completion to Jerry Jeudy that set up Andre Szmyt's tying 51-yard field goal with eight seconds left in regulation; Cleveland has dropped two straight and hosts Houston on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Crew open Round One at Inter Miami on Nov. 21; FC Cincinnati's Wild Card is Nov. 19
briefs.summary: ESPN's MLS schedule, read this morning, lists Game 1 of the Columbus Crew's best-of-three Round One series at Inter Miami for Saturday, Nov. 21, at 6 p.m. ET at Nu Stadium in Miami on Apple TV, the first date the series has carried; FC Cincinnati's single-elimination Wild Card match at Orlando City stays Thursday, Nov. 19, at 7:30 p.m. ET, and the same listing has a to-be-determined visitor at top-seeded Nashville on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 4 p.m. ET, the Round One slot the Wild Card winner fills.

briefs.headline: Hoshoryu forces down Asanoyama for a second straight win at the Kyushu basho
briefs.summary: Yokozuna (grand champion) Hoshoryu, back after right knee surgery kept him out of September's tournament and the end of July's, beat maegashira (rank-and-file) 1 Asanoyama by yoritaoshi (force out and down) in 5.1 seconds in the final bout of day 2 at the Fukuoka Kokusai Center, taking a left front-mawashi grip, letting go of his overarm hold and swinging Asanoyama off balance with a right underarm throw before driving him down; he said he had been nervous on day 1 after the long layoff and could concentrate on day 2. Hoshoryu has won all six meetings with Asanoyama, who had beaten ozeki (champion) Aonishiki on day 1.

briefs.headline: Onosato survives his own pull as both yokozuna and all three ozeki win on day 2
briefs.summary: Yokozuna Onosato, beaten on day 1, got his right hand inside against maegashira 1 Fujiryoga, then pressed down on his head and pulled, drawing Fujiryoga into his chest and onto the edge before he circled, got the right arm back in and won by yorikiri (force out) in 9.6 seconds; Kasugano, the former sekiwake Tochinowaka commentating for NHK, said pulling while pressing the head is something a yokozuna must not do. Ozeki Aonishiki beat Yoshinofuji, day 1's conqueror of Onosato, by uchimuso (inner thigh twist down) in 5.0 seconds, Kotozakura slapped down Churanoumi in 4.2 seconds and Kirishima forced out Fujiseiun for his second win; chief judge Kokonoe, the former ozeki Chiyotaikai, said it was not a day with an upset in the air.

briefs.headline: Fujinokawa falls to a second straight loss; Tamawashi, 41, passes Kisenosato with his 715th win
briefs.summary: Sekiwake Fujinokawa, 21, who wanted this tournament to build a case for ozeki promotion after 11 wins in September, was caught at the tachiai (initial charge) by maegashira 3 Takayasu, who locked his arms and walked him out by kimedashi (arm-lock force out) in 8.7 seconds. Tamawashi, 41, the oldest man to return to the top division since the Showa era, thrust out Tokihayate for his first win and his 715th in makuuchi (the top division), moving past the former yokozuna Kisenosato into 7th on the all-time list a week before his 42nd birthday; Nikkan Sports' results table has eight men unbeaten after two days, among them Hoshoryu, Kirishima, Atamifuji and Takanosho. In juryo (the second division), Wakatakakage pushed out Namatame for a second win since returning from four leg operations, and Hishoshi withdrew with a fractured left eye socket, the second kyujo (absence) in the top two divisions.

briefs.headline: Giants beat the Eagles 19-11 in Philadelphia and hand them a 7th straight loss
briefs.summary: Jameis Winston, in for J.J. McCarthy after a hip injury, threw the go-ahead touchdown pass, and the Giants won in Philadelphia for the first time since October 2013, ending a run of 13 straight Eagles home wins in the series; New York (five wins, two losses and a tie) is the only NFC East team with a winning record. The Eagles are on their longest losing streak since eight straight in Andy Reid's last season in 2012, with Jalen Hurts likely out for the year with blood clots, and could remake the roster at Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET trade deadline.

briefs.headline: Love accounts for 4 touchdowns as the Packers beat the Patriots 45-27 in Foxborough
briefs.summary: Jordan Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns and ran for another, Christian Watson caught seven passes for 171 yards and Matthew Golden 10 for 164, and Green Bay scored 21 points off four New England turnovers, two of them Xavier McKinney interceptions; the Packers had not scored 45 with 450 yards since Nov. 11, 1962, and have won five of six. Mike Vrabel said there were no two ways around how badly New England was beaten, and the Patriots dropped to five wins and four losses.

briefs.headline: Bears beat the Buccaneers 27-24 on a last-second field goal despite 5 turnovers
briefs.summary: Caleb Williams threw a career-high four interceptions and Luther Burden III lost a fumble that set up Bucky Irving's tying touchdown and Baker Mayfield's 2-point run, but Williams found Colston Loveland for 38 yards in the final minute and Cairo Santos kicked a 38-yarder as time expired on Sunday night in Chicago; it was the Bears' first win with five or more turnovers since December 2006, and they have not trailed in four straight wins. The Bears have seven wins and two losses, and Buffalo visits Minnesota tonight at 8:15 p.m. ET to close Week 9.

briefs.headline: Reaves scores 43 without Doncic as the Lakers win 121-116 at Detroit
briefs.summary: Austin Reaves made 14 of 27 shots and all 11 free throws, and hit a one-legged, off-balance 3-pointer as the shot clock ran out in the final minute to end Detroit's comeback from 26 down, with Luka Doncic, who had averaged 45 points over the previous four games, sitting out; Walker Kessler had 12 points and 16 rebounds. The Lakers lead the Western Conference with nine wins and two losses and play at Atlanta tonight, a half game ahead of the Spurs, who are at Phoenix.

briefs.headline: 76ers win 127-121 in Chicago for their best 11-game start since 2000-01
briefs.summary: Jaylen Brown scored 29, Tyrese Maxey 27 and LeBron James a season-high 22, with Joel Embiid adding 18 points and 10 rebounds, as Philadelphia held off a Bulls team that got 19 points and 15 assists from Josh Giddey; the 76ers have nine wins and two losses and lead the East, and James' early 3-pointer made him the leading scorer in history against the Bulls, passing Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. Chicago has lost seven straight, and Brown faces his former club for the first time in a game that counts when Boston visits Philadelphia on Tuesday; the Bulls host the Spurs on Wednesday.

briefs.headline: Celtics rout the Bucks 117-97 and drop Milwaukee to its worst start since 1993-94
briefs.summary: Paul George scored 27 and Jayson Tatum 21, sitting out the fourth quarter, after Boston answered a 14-point first-quarter deficit with 18 unanswered points and led by 13 at halftime; Kyle Kuzma had 27 for Milwaukee, which has one win in 10 games, its worst opening since the 1993-94 team lost 10 of its first 11. Boston has eight wins and two losses on a four-game trip that goes to Philadelphia on Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Manchester United come back twice for a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa and stay 18th
briefs.summary: Villa led through Alysson and Nicolas Jackson inside four minutes and 4-2 after John McGinn's penalty and Leon Goretzka's goal, but Joshua Zirkzee scored in the second minute of stoppage time and Patrick Dorgu headed in Bruno Fernandes' corner in the sixth, after Fernandes' penalty and Youri Tielemans had levelled the first half; United go into the international break in the relegation zone with one win in 10. Unai Emery left the dugout before the equaliser and told Sky Sports the match was finishing when it came, with Villa 10th.

briefs.headline: Brighton beat 10-man Brentford 2-0 and climb to 2nd in the Premier League
briefs.summary: Diego Gomez's left-footed strike from more than 25 yards in the 15th minute and Pascal Gross' 42nd-minute penalty, for Keane Lewis-Potter's shirt pull on Luka Vuskovic, gave Brighton a seventh win in 10 league matches after Brentford's Igor Thiago was sent off in the 23rd for catching Chema Andres in the face with a raised arm; Brighton have 22 points, five behind Arsenal, and moved above Manchester City on the day City had no match.

briefs.headline: Swayman makes 40 saves as the Bruins beat the Panthers 4-1 in a 126-penalty-minute game
briefs.summary: Elias Lindholm, Mikey Eyssimont and Morgan Geekie scored in a first period that opened with Nikita Zadorov fighting Brady Tkachuk at the first faceoff, and Jeremy Swayman stopped 40 shots, 17 in the first, for a Boston team that is unbeaten in seven home games and has won four straight a day after putting James Hagens on injured reserve; Carter Verhaeghe scored on the power play for Florida, which has lost three of four and had swept Boston last season.

briefs.headline: Hellebuyck's first shutout for New Jersey beats Toronto 4-0; the Devils have won 9 of 10
briefs.summary: Connor Hellebuyck made 23 saves in Toronto and became the first goalie in Devils history to win each of his first five games with the club after last month's trade from Winnipeg, where New Jersey plays Tuesday without him, general manager Sunny Mehta said; Timo Meier scored twice in the second period, Nico Hischier added a power-play goal and Connor Brown an empty-netter. The Maple Leafs have lost three straight.

briefs.headline: Georgia takes over at No. 1 in the AP poll as Miami falls to 5th
briefs.summary: Georgia received 53 first-place votes in the AP Top 25 released Sunday after beating Ole Miss in Oxford, with Utah 2nd on 12 first-place votes, Notre Dame 3rd on five and UCLA 4th; Miami dropped from first to 5th after losing at Notre Dame, Texas Tech rose three places to 10th after holding off West Virginia, and BYU fell five to 12th after losing at Utah. The second College Football Playoff ranking comes Tuesday night.

waters.reading: 48.8 cfs, 1.29 feet at 5:15 a.m., falling on flow against 56.2 cfs and steady on stage against 1.35 feet in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.working: Against Sunday's edition reading of 52.4 cfs and 1.32 feet at 5:15 a.m. the gauge is down 3.6 cfs and 0.03 feet on the day, and the recession has taken another step: the USGS record held 52.4 from 3:30 a.m. Sunday, with one 15-minute flicker to 53.7 at 3:15, dropped to 51.2 at 10:15 a.m., to 50.0 at 6 p.m. with a single return to 51.2 at 6:45, and reached 48.8 at 11:45 p.m., trading places with 50.0 until 1 a.m. Monday and holding 48.8 since; the stage went 1.32, 1.31, 1.30, 1.29 on the same steps. The fetcher's 24-hour comparison figures, 56.2 and 1.35, are Saturday morning's values, a 48-hour window, so the day's true change is the 3.6 cfs above. At 48.8 the Williams is at the lowest reading of the fall for a second straight morning, under Sunday's 52.4 and Thursday's 54.9, on a slide that ran from 1,360 cfs on Oct. 15 through 653 on Oct. 17, 141 on Oct. 24 and 70.7 on Oct. 31. The read string is the fetcher's own verdict, printed as it stands, "49 cfs - prime wading water." Stocking: WVDNR's fish-stocking page refused this morning's fetch with a Cloudflare block, so no stocking line runs; the river's most recent stocking this paper has reported is Oct. 29. At 49 cfs and clear the Williams is the file's low-water problem at its lowest yet: pocket water and plunge pools shrunk to their cores, every fish in the deepest slot of each pocket, the water cold and glass-clear, and a wading angler the loudest thing on the river. Structure is pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks; forage is caddis, stoneflies and sculpin. So: a long leader, nine to 12 feet to 6X or 7X, and small flies, a size 16 to 18 caddis pupa or a size 18 soft-hackle swung into the plunge-pool tailouts, a size 16 to 18 pheasant tail or small black stonefly nymph under a tiny indicator or a dry-dropper through the pocket seams, a size 20 to 22 blue-winged olive on top through the warmest part of an overcast afternoon, and for the one bigger fish in each plunge pool a size 8 to 10 olive or black sculpin pattern fished on a short line into the foam at the head of the pool at first or last light, before the sun gets on it; an egg pattern or a San Juan worm under a small indicator still covers the holdover stocked pools. The heavy-nymph-on-the-seam game is for 500 cfs, a number this river has not seen since the 653 of Oct. 17.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.69 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 24.8 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 24.7 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Against Sunday's edition reading of 24.55 at 5 a.m. the pool is up 0.14 on the day, and the day in between reversed the week's drawdown for an afternoon: the trace climbed from 24.90 at 12:15 p.m. Sunday to 25.00 at 2 p.m., touched 25.13 at 2:30, held between 25.02 and 25.09 through the afternoon, spiked to 25.18 at 6:15 p.m., then eased to 24.95 by 9 p.m., 24.83 at 11:45 p.m., 24.75 at 1:15 a.m. and 24.69 at 5 a.m. Monday. Nothing in the traces says rain, the Williams having fallen all day, so the half-foot was the dam holding water back through the afternoon and letting it down again overnight, not the hills; whether that is a lockage rhythm or the start of a scheduled change the trace does not say, and this paper will not guess. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 24.7 the gauge is more than two feet under the up-and-pushing line at 27. A pool that rose and fell half a foot in 12 hours still fishes the structure, not the slack: wing dams, riprap and the lock wall are the file's structure, shad and skipjack with crawfish in the rock the forage. A white or pearl three-and-a-half to four-inch swimbait on a half-ounce head or a three-quarter-ounce spoon down the current face of each wing dam at first light for hybrids and white bass; a crawfish-colored jig or a three-inch tube dragged slow on the riprap through the middle of the day for smallmouth and drum; and with the water cooling through November a half-ounce blade bait or a jig and minnow worked vertical along the lock wall seam and the barge-cut edges for sauger, cut skipjack on the bottom in the cuts after dark for blue catfish. The overnight fall pulls the shad off the flats and onto the wing-dam faces, which puts the first hour of light on the rock.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.28 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 26.11 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.3 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Against Sunday's edition reading of 26.04 at 5 a.m. the gauge is up 0.24 on the day, and the sawtooth climbed through Sunday evening: the trace ran 26.02 to 26.14 through the early afternoon, 26.17 to 26.25 from 5 to 7:30 p.m., reached 26.40 at 9:45 p.m., and swung between 26.25 and 26.40 every quarter hour from then to dawn, 26.28 at 5 a.m. Monday. The dam below tells the rest: the USGS gauge at Ironton, Ohio, below Greenup Dam, recorded Greenup's discharge between 14,900 and 23,700 cfs through Sunday afternoon, 27,400 at 7:15 p.m., 26,600 at 10:15 and 27,100 at 11:45 p.m., then 19,500 to 26,200 through the small hours and 22,100 at 5 a.m. Monday, the Ironton stage rising from 34.22 at 12:30 p.m. Sunday to 34.61 at 11:45 p.m. and reading 34.50 at 5 a.m. So Greenup passed more water Sunday evening than it had Saturday night, the Ironton pool came up four-tenths, and the Huntington reach came up a quarter of a foot with it while the Byrd pool above was being held and released; the two moves are of a piece, and neither is rain. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access. Below the dam the reach is a quarter-foot over Sunday morning with Greenup drawing 22,100 cfs below, a little more push on the seams than Sunday, and the fishing still goes to them: a white swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon down the current face of the wing dams at first light for hybrids and white bass, a half-ounce blade bait or a chartreuse-and-white paddletail on a half-ounce head worked slow along the lock wall's downstream edge for sauger, a crawfish jig on the riprap at midday, and cut skipjack on the bottom in the slack beside the discharge after dark for blue and flathead catfish. No color in either trace; the slack-behind-the-dams game is for a muddy river, not this one.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 1:41 AM at 0.3 ft, high 7:48 AM at 4.3 ft, low 2:29 PM at 0.6 ft, high 8:02 PM at 3.4 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: low 12:24 AM at 0.2 ft, high 6:59 AM at 5.5 ft, low 1:24 PM at 0.3 ft, high 7:16 PM at 4.0 ft. Water 65.7F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:30 a.m. Moon new, 0% illuminated, 29.1 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 7:48 AM and 8:02 PM in the sound.
waters.working: All four of the sound's events land inside the calendar day, the 1:41 a.m. low behind us at press time, and so do the surf's, the 12:24 a.m. low at Ocean City Beach pier having come an hour and 17 minutes ahead of the sound's; the sound lags the surf 49 minutes on the morning high, 65 on the midday low and 46 on the evening high, the long-lag-on-the-ebb pattern the reference describes. The ranges are at the top of the cycle: a 4.0-foot fill overnight from 0.3 to this morning's 4.3, a 3.7-foot drain to 2:29 p.m., a 2.8-foot fill to the 8:02 p.m. high, which at 3.4 is a tenth under Sunday's evening high, and the surf's 5.5 morning high matches Sunday's; the moon is new today at 0%, so these are spring tides at their peak and the inlet runs hardest either side of slack. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, reads 65.7F, down 1.0 on Sunday's 66.7 and 2.5 under Saturday's 68.2, a second straight morning of cooling. What's running: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry report for November, published Sunday, Nov. 1, is eight days old this morning, a monthly report and not today's conditions. It has the Jolly Roger Pier starting to see scattered speckled trout, with night bottom fishing producing Virginia mullet and spot and bluefish thick in the early mornings; Surf City Pier with pompano, black drum and croaker on the bottom, casting shots at Spanish and bluefish, and king mackerel good before the last blow; East Coast Sports with the piers catching big red drum of 32 inches and more, mostly on the north end, smaller reds and some trout inside, and trout to pick up as it cools; Native Son with the wind scattering bait, the five- to eight-foot seams of the main creeks the depth to work for trout, cut bait the best red drum bait, and false albacore possible; Capt. Ricky Kellum with many small specks and some to 28 inches on live shrimp under a cork in four to eight feet of water, light jigheads for the artificials, and black drum and small reds on the same floated shrimp; Carolina Flats with topwater early to find the trout schools, deeper holes later, and reds in a last blitz on the oyster and grass banks on soft plastics before the bait thins; and the boats with kings on slow-trolled bait in 50 to 60 feet, bluefish, false albacore and gray trout on nearshore structure, sea bass and triggerfish on the bottom in 60 to 80 feet. Beach conditions: no NWS Wilmington product was active for coastal Pender or Onslow, the Topsail point or the adjacent marine zones at 5:44 a.m.; the only North Carolina product on the wire was a Frost Advisory from the Greenville-Spartanburg office for Piedmont and foothill counties to 9 a.m. Tide is the whole game, and this morning it is the last of the flood at press time: the sound fills to 4.3 at 7:48 a.m. and then drains for six and three-quarter hours to the 2:29 p.m. low, the longest morning ebb of the cycle on the new-moon tide. Structure here is oyster bars, grass edges, dock lights and the ICWW channel, forage mud minnows, shrimp and finger mullet, which is the report's live-shrimp-and-small-plastic fishing. Trout first: a topwater plug over the flooded grass edges in the first hour of light around the 7:48 a.m. high, then a 3/16- or quarter-ounce jighead with a paddletail or soft jerkbait worked slow down the five- to eight-foot seams where the creek channels drop into the ICWW as the drain gathers through mid-morning, and a popping cork with live shrimp over the oyster bars on the first of the flood after 3 p.m. and again either side of the 8:02 p.m. high; with the water at Beaufort under 66F the trout hold the deeper holes on the midday low. Red drum want the last of the fall, which on this table is roughly noon to the 2:29 p.m. low, cut menhaden or a finger mullet on a quarter-ounce head a couple of feet off the creek-channel edges as the grass drains; the dusk high at 8:02 p.m. puts drum up on the flooded grass and oyster banks for a weedless gold spoon or a soft plastic, and the ebb that follows runs under the dock lights past 1 a.m., the report's small plastics or a suspending twitchbait where the shrimp and finger mullet stack. Spot and sea mullet on bloodworm or shrimp on a two-hook bottom rig in the ICWW channel an hour either side of the evening high. Bluefish are the early-morning fish on the beach behind the bait pods on a metal jig or topwater, per both piers. Flounder are release only.
